title: Evaluating Generate–Validate–Repair Pipelines for Intent‑to‑Configuration NetOps Tasks: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a single‑shot LLM configuration generator against a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline (with a canary/repair stage) on a 1000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus (2000 paired episodes). The declared model was gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses) and validation used a deterministic digital‑twin validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics exactly one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by both arms; downstream validation and the permitted single repair call (guarded arm only) were the only mechanisms for paired outcome differences. Observed outcomes: baseline safe‑deploy = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded safe‑deploy = 1000/1000 = 1.000; paired difference = 0.005 (n11=995, n10=5, n01=0, n00=0). The preregistered primary inferential test (exact two‑sided McNemar) yields p = 0.0625 (not < 0.05). The preregistered paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) is [0.001, 0.01]. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred and total model calls used = 1005 (shared_initial = 1000; repair = 5). We report the exact McNemar result as the preregistered confirmatory outcome, present the bootstrap CI as a preregistered descriptive summary, and explicitly label any one‑sided tests as exploratory since they were not prespecified.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→configuration translation for network operations promises operational efficiency but risks multi‑step sequencing errors, transient invariant violations, and protected‑field interference that can produce harmful outcomes. Prior empirical and survey work documents LLM hallucination, prompt sensitivity, and structured‑output failures that reduce correctness for code and configuration tasks; this motivates architectures that pair generative models with deterministic validators and bounded repair procedures [1],[2].

This paper reports a preregistered, artifact‑grounded paired experiment (cand‑003‑stud‑001) that isolates purely downstream validator/repair effects under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Our precise research question: when baseline and guarded conditions begin from the exact same sampled initial candidate (shared_initial_candidate semantics), to what degree can a downstream deterministic validator plus a single allowed repair call (guarded pipeline with a canary stage) improve paired safe‑deploy outcomes compared with reusing the same initial candidate unmodified (baseline)? The design intentionally isolates downstream interventions so any paired difference is attributable to validation and permitted repair rather than to first‑pass prompt, sampling, or decoding differences.

Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired experiment (Npairs = 1000) with deterministic task selection from a synthetic challenging_workflow_stress_v1 corpus and archived validator traces; (2) artifact‑grounded execution accounting and preregistered confirmatory analysis using an exact two‑sided McNemar test plus preregistered descriptive bootstrap summaries; (3) concrete operational diagnosis of why a preregistered power assumption mismatched the observed baseline and what that implies for measuring downstream verifier/repair benefits under shared_initial_candidate semantics.
sections.related_work:
Prior studies report frequent LLM hallucinations and prompt sensitivity that materially affect generated artifacts including code and configuration, motivating verifier‑assisted workflows [1],[2]. Constrained or schema‑aware decoding reduces syntactic and executable errors in structured domains, though much empirical evidence comes from non‑NetOps domains and requires high‑fidelity validators to generalize to networking [3]. Recent NetOps and agentic‑AI system work describe generate→validate→repair prototypes, protocol‑mediated governance, and proof‑carrying/audit proposals that aim to mitigate automation risks, and they emphasize that operational reliability depends on validator coverage and externally enforced protocols rather than on any single model alone [4],[5],[6].

Our study complements these works by preregistering a paired comparison whose estimand isolates the incremental effect of deterministic downstream validation and a single limited repair call when the initial candidate is held constant across conditions.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. The study preregistration (cand‑003‑stud‑001) was finalized and frozen prior to any hosted‑model invocation; the preregistration SHA‑256 recorded in the execution manifest is ab4c6436c6ece56bf47da7730d50485a17cdb9bb86a90a4231042303d3b489ec. Key preregistered elements: confirmatory paired binary design; task_count = 1000 deterministic tasks drawn from the challenging_workflow_stress_v1 synthetic corpus; generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (exactly one sampled initial generation per pair deterministically reused by both conditions); initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; primary test = exact two‑sided McNemar. Secondary preregistered summaries: paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729) and sensitivity analyses treating failed calls as unsafe.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and interpretive consequences. Because generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate both baseline and guarded episodes begin from the same sampled initial candidate; the guarded pipeline may reject the candidate via deterministic validation and may invoke at most one permitted repair call. Under this choice, paired outcome differences can only arise from deterministic validator decisions and permitted repair(s). The design therefore does not measure effects that would arise from independent first‑pass generations, alternative prompts, or constrained decoding arms that were not executed.

Model/runtime configuration and temperature caveat. The declared provider/model (execution/model_configuration.json) is gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses). The archived model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. The orchestration adapter was hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and the deterministic digital‑twin validator was deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator enforces workflow policies, command order, protected‑field noninterference and returns a deterministic safe‑deploy verdict). The task manifest schema included initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and difficulty labels.

Execution, missingness, and analysis plan. The preregistration limited retries (maximum_attempts_per_call = 1) and prespecified missingness treatments (primary: complete_pair_primary; sensitivity: failures_as_zero). The confirmatory analysis executor was the preregistered paired_binary_analysis_v1 implementing an exact two‑sided McNemar on the 2×2 contingency table; the paired bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) was preregistered as a descriptive secondary summary. Multiplicity for secondary hypotheses was preregistered (Holm–Bonferroni) but no additional confirmatory claims were made.
sections.results:
Execution accounting (artifact‑grounded). The run started 2026‑09‑01T06:31:07Z and completed 2026‑09‑01T08:38:57Z. Planned episodes = 2000; completed = 2000; complete_pairs = 1000; failed episodes = 0. Provider audit shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 1005 with stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation = 1000, repair = 5} and cache_miss_count = 1005; all deterministic consistency checks passed (see deterministic_reconciliation.json).

Primary paired outcomes and preregistered inferential test. The 2×2 paired contingency table is: n11 = 995 (both succeeded), n10 = 5 (guarded succeeded, baseline failed), n01 = 0 (baseline succeeded, guarded failed), n00 = 0 (both failed). Observed success rates: baseline = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded = 1000/1000 = 1.000; observed paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered primary confirmatory test (exact two‑sided McNemar) returns p = 0.0625; this does not meet the preregistered two‑sided α = 0.05, so the preregistered H1 is not supported.

Preregistered secondary descriptive summaries and exploratory statistics. The preregistered paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) yields [0.001, 0.01]. A one‑sided McNemar (guarded > baseline) yields p = 0.03125; because a one‑sided test was NOT prespecified in cand‑003‑stud‑001 it is reported explicitly as exploratory/post‑hoc. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred (repair stage_count = 5); total model calls used = 1005 (shared_initial = 1000; repair calls = 5). Representative episode artifacts illustrating repair traces and validator acceptance/rejection are archived under execution/scoring and execution/responses.

Inferential hierarchy and bootstrap sensitivity (requested clarification). The exact two‑sided McNemar test is the preregistered confirmatory analysis and it failed to reject at two‑sided α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). The paired bootstrap CI and any one‑sided McNemar calculations are preregistered descriptive/exploratory summaries or explicitly post‑hoc and therefore do not overturn the preregistered confirmatory null decision. The bootstrap CI may exclude zero in this regime because bootstrap percentile intervals on the paired difference can be sensitive to extremely sparse discordant counts (here n10=5, n01=0) and to the resampling procedure; the bootstrap was run with seed = 1729 and 10,000 resamples as preregistered, which produces the reported descriptive interval but does not change the confirmatory McNemar outcome.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation within the preregistered design. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics any paired improvement must originate from downstream deterministic validation and the allowed single repair call; our artifact‑grounded run shows five successful repair invocations that converted specific failing initial candidates into accepted candidates. The small absolute paired gain (0.005) and the discrete exact McNemar p‑value (0.0625) reflect the observed data regime: near‑unity baseline success produced very few discordant pairs, limiting the power of the preregistered two‑sided paired test.

Power mismatch and practical consequences. The preregistered power_and_precision_plan assumed baseline ≈ 0.60 and targeted an absolute increase of 0.15; the observed baseline (0.995) lies far above that assumption. This mismatch substantially reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute gains under McNemar’s test because discordant pairs become rare. Consequently, the absence of two‑sided statistical significance here does not imply absence of practically useful repair effects in contexts with higher baseline failure prevalence.

Threats to validity. Construct validity depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5’s rule coverage: unmodeled semantic or emergent multi‑device policy violations would not be detected and would inflate measured success. Internal validity benefits from deterministic seeding and completed pairs = 1000, but by design the paired estimand omits first‑pass generation variation (shared_initial_candidate). External validity is limited by the synthetic corpus and single evaluated model (gpt‑5‑mini), so generalization across devices, vendors, or model families requires follow‑ups.

Recommended preregistered follow‑ups. Artifact‑grounded follow‑ups supported by the archive: (1) relax shared_initial_candidate to measure first‑pass prompt/decoding interventions; (2) sweep repair budgets (0..k) to quantify marginal returns per failure class; (3) expand validator rule sets and topology heterogeneity to probe external validity; (4) evaluate multiple model families to map model dependence. Each follow‑up should preregister power calculations aligned to plausible baseline failure rates.
sections.conclusion:
In a preregistered paired study (Npairs = 1000) that held initial model generations constant across arms (shared_initial_candidate), a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small absolute paired improvement (0.005) relative to a baseline single‑shot generator; the preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test did not reach α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred and total model calls used = 1005. The confirmatory claim is the preregistered two‑sided McNemar outcome; bootstrap intervals and any one‑sided statistics are reported as descriptive/exploratory and do not overturn the preregistered confirmatory result. Artifact archives (preregistration, execution manifest, raw responses, validator traces, and analysis artifacts) accompany the run to support reproducibility and to guide prespecified follow‑ups that broaden model diversity, validator coverage, and repair budgets.

figure_captions: Figure 1: Paired safe‑deploy rates per condition (baseline vs guarded). Bars show observed proportions with point estimates; the bootstrap 95% percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) is shown as error bars and reported as a secondary descriptive summary.

Figure 2: Paired bootstrap distribution of the paired difference (guarded − baseline) from the preregistered executor (histogram with 95% percentile CI bounds). This visualization supplements the preregistered exact McNemar confirmatory test and illustrates bootstrap sensitivity to sparse discordant counts.

Table 2: Primary estimand results — paired contingency and inferential outcomes (n11 = 995; n10 = 5; n01 = 0; n00 = 0; baseline = 995/1000; guarded = 1000/1000; difference = 0.005; exact two‑sided McNemar p = 0.0625; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.001, 0.01]).
disclosure_statement: Declared model and provider: gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses). Orchestration and validator: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 with deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as the deterministic digital‑twin validator. Preregistration: cand‑003‑stud‑001 (frozen prior to any model calls; preregistration SHA‑256 = ab4c6436c6ece56bf47da7730d50485a17cdb9bb86a90a4231042303d3b489ec). Immutable initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). After the autonomy lock, literature review, experiment design, execution, analysis, and manuscript drafting were performed by the autonomous run; no human manually edited the manuscript's technical content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Single‑model scope: only the declared model gpt‑5‑mini was evaluated; results do not generalize across model families or versions.

Synthetic corpus and deterministic validator: tasks come from a synthetic stress corpus and validation used a deterministic digital twin (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); external validity to heterogeneous vendor/legacy environments is limited.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the paired comparison isolates downstream validator/repair effects only; it does not measure differences that would arise from independent first‑pass generations or alternative prompting arms that were not executed (those arms were not part of the frozen preregistration).

Low baseline failure prevalence: baseline success = 99.5%; the preregistered power plan assumed baseline≈0.60 and a target effect of 0.15, so the observed baseline greatly reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute gains. This mismatch is reported explicitly and reduces the study's ability to detect very small practical effects using the preregistered confirmatory test.
Sparse repairs and interpretation limits: only five validator repairs were invoked, constraining inference about repair efficacy across failure modes.

Statistical nuance: the preregistered primary test is exact two‑sided McNemar (p = 0.0625). The paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.001, 0.01] is a preregistered descriptive summary but is sensitive to sparse discordant counts; a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) was computed post‑hoc and is explicitly labeled exploratory because it was not prespecified in the frozen preregistration.

Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary depends on the emulator/validator's rule set; semantic and emergent multi‑device policy violations may be underrepresented in the validator's modeled constraints.
